summary: AstroCuy: Mission Trainer is an interactive lunar simulator designed to spark children's curiosity about space exploration and teach them how real astronauts operate during Moon missions. Developed for the Junior Astronaut challenge, the game features a charming pixel-art guinea pig astronaut ("AstroCuy") and an engaging introductory story to capture young learners' attention right from the start. Starting in Phase 1 (Lunar Simulator), kids navigate the lunar environment using intuitive controls (WASD), interact with mission equipment (E), and consult a real-time Mission Panel (H) grounded in authentic NASA protocols. By blending retro-inspired storytelling with hands-on exploration, AstroCuy turns space science into an accessible, investigative adventure for future explorers.
details:
What does it do & How does it work?

AstroCuy: Mission Trainer is a browser-based interactive lunar simulation (Phase 1) where children step into the role of a Junior Astronaut alongside a guinea pig companion. Through an introductory narrative and hands-on tasks on the Moon, players move around the environment (WASD), interact with spacecraft and lunar equipment (E), and review real astronaut procedures via an in-game Mission Panel (H).

Benefits & Educational Impact:

Traditional space documentation can feel overly complex for children. By introducing a relatable, culturally inspired mascot ("AstroCuy") and gamified challenges, the project lowers the barrier to entry and motivates kids to actively investigate how real astronauts live, train, and solve problems in space.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used:

Developed using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and WebGL/3D web rendering technologies, combining retro pixel-art UI elements with interactive 3D models (GLB/FBX) optimized to run smoothly in any standard web browser without installations.

Creativity & Design Factors:

Our team prioritized child-friendly UX/UI, intuitive keyboard controls, clear visual feedback, and scientific accuracy aligned with NASA lunar mission training.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI):

AI tools (GitHub Copilot, Claude, and Gemini) were used transparently to assist with code structuring, debugging, and translating/adapting educational English texts for children, as well as initial 3D asset prototyping. All core game mechanics, educational design, and final integration were developed and verified by our team.
